findings.title: Total page count is off by one for exact multiples of the page size
findings.body: totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. For a group with exactly 100 members and limit 50 this reports 3 pages instead of 2, so showingLast is false on the real last page and the Next action advances offset to 100, fetching and displaying an empty page. It should use a ceiling calculation, e.g. Math.ceil(user_count / limit) for non-zero counts.

findings.title: Public group members page now silently shows only the first 50 members
findings.body: The members action now always paginates with the client's default limit of 50, whereas non-automatic groups previously returned all members. The public group/members template and GroupMembers route were not given any pagination controls or follow-up fetching, so members beyond the first 50 of a large group are unreachable in the public UI.

findings.title: Members pagination parameters are not validated or clamped
findings.body: limit and offset are taken directly from request params via to_i. A request such as members.json?limit=-1 or offset=-1 can produce a database error/500, limit=0 returns a meta limit of 0 that breaks client page calculations, and a huge limit lets any user who can see a group serialize its entire membership in one request, defeating the new pagination and creating an expensive response for large automatic groups. Clamp limit to a sane range and offset to at least 0.

findings.title: Creating a group silently discards the selected alias level
findings.body: The client sends alias_level in Group#asJSON and the group form shows the alias-level selector for unsaved groups, but Admin::GroupsController#create only assigns name and visible. A newly created group therefore always gets the default alias_level regardless of what the admin selected; #update handles alias_level, so create should assign it too.

findings.title: PATCH membership updates are now ignored and flip group visibility off
findings.body: The old PATCH branch that applied changes:{add,delete} has been removed, but Rails still routes PATCH to #update. A legacy/API PATCH request now ignores its membership changes, and because line 38 unconditionally sets visible = (params[:visible] == "true"), a PATCH that does not include visible silently makes the group invisible while returning success. Either keep handling PATCH changes or reject unsupported PATCH/partial updates instead of applying the visibility default.

findings.title: Automatic-group remove_member spec uses the wrong HTTP verb
findings.body: The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' example calls xhr :put, :remove_member, but the route added in config/routes.rb and the successful removal example use DELETE. Because controller specs dispatch directly to the action and bypass routing, this example passes even if the DELETE route is broken or removed, so it does not test the endpoint clients actually call.
